# Await every tool call; arguments are keyword-only and omitted optional arguments default to None. Nested object arguments are plain dicts.
# ToolResult = {ok: bool, data: the tool's structured result or None, text: str, files: list[{path: str, line1: int, line2: int, content: str}], diffs: list[dict], images: list[{image: str, index: int}], images_dropped: int, error: str | None, truncated: bool}. Check ok and truncated.
# Constants: PROJECT_ROOT, CHAT_ID, WORKSPACE_DIR, ARTIFACTS_DIR, RUNS_DIR, RUN_ID, RUN_DIR: str; PARENT_ARTIFACTS_DIR: str | None (None without a parent or when the parent has no Python workspace yet).
def help(name: str | None = None) -> str: ...  # one function's full typed signature, parameter docs and data types; no name: the function index
def tools() -> list[str]: ...
def host_path(p: str) -> str: ...
def virtual_path(p: str) -> str: ...
def show(value: Any, *, kind: Literal["table", "markdown", "bar", "line", "area", "scatter", "pie"] | None = None, title: str | None = None, x: str | None = None, y: str | list[str] | None = None, columns: list[str] | None = None) -> None: ...  # show a table, chart or markdown to the user; you only get a one-line note back
# Monty restricted Python. Imports: annotationlib,asyncio,base64,binascii,bisect,collections,copy,csv,dataclasses,datetime,decimal,fnmatch,functools,hashlib,itertools,json,math,os,os.path,pathlib,posixpath,random,re,sys,time,tomllib,typing,unicodedata. Missing: ast,shutil,socket,subprocess,threading,urllib. Path.relative_to missing; paths are not orderable (sort with key=str); with_suffix/rglob, os.walk and os.path.join/relpath/splitext available (partial CPython APIs). globals() is missing. Bound methods cannot be passed as values (max(d, key=d.get) fails; use key=lambda k: d[k]); calling d.get(k, 0) works. No third-party/network/subprocess. A script can import its own .py files from PROJECT_ROOT (no relative imports, no sys.path).
# Tool functions are async and take keyword arguments: the same arguments as the direct tool of the same name. Each returns ToolResult. name(a, b, …) lists the required arguments; … means optional ones exist. After -> come the keys of data: key? may be missing or None, key[] is a list, key[{…}] a list of dicts, key{…} a dict, {*} arbitrary keys. help("name") prints the full typed signature and data types.
shell(command, description, …) -> {stdout}
